article_title: A Study of Geometry Content Knowledge of Elementary Preservice Teachers
citation: Fatma Aslan-Tutak and Thomasenia Lott Adams. (2015). A Study of Geometry Content Knowledge of Elementary Preservice Teachers. International Electronic Journal of Elementary Education, 7(3), 301-318. https://www.iejee.com
title: Mathematical Knowledge for Teaching (MKT) model with six domains of teacher content knowledge
description: The article frames teacher knowledge using Shulman's model and Ball and colleagues' MKT model, which "addresses how a teacher uses mathematics for teaching." Under subject matter knowledge sit common content knowledge, specialized content knowledge, and horizon content knowledge; under pedagogical content knowledge sit knowledge of content and students, of content and teaching, and of content and curriculum. The study's instrument (CKT-M Measures) derives from this research continuum, and the article argues preservice teachers need specialized content knowledge — mathematics for teaching — not just factual knowledge.
requirements: The model distinguishes knowledge unique to teaching from knowledge not unique to teaching, so use requires attending to that distinction
constraints: The article applies the model to elementary geometry content knowledge for preservice teachers in a methods course setting
target_learning_goals: specialized content knowledge of geometry for teaching
examples: The CKT-M Measures geometry section, developed by Learning Mathematics for Teaching at University of Michigan, was used to measure change in geometry content knowledge
